problem: Topological planners for VLN-CE (e.g. ETPNav) build graphs with a fixed node-merging threshold and a static geometric-distance bias in the Graph Transformer. They over-sample simple areas, under-sample complex ones, and favor geometrically near but semantically wrong nodes ('navigational myopia').
motivation: Scene complexity varies along a trajectory, so a fixed graph granularity mismatches it: redundant nodes add noise in corridors, while too few candidates in open or junction areas hurt precision. Geometric proximity also does not imply instruction correctness, for example turning at the first door when told to take the second left.
key_idea: Adapt graph granularity online by setting the node-merging threshold from the angular dispersion of predicted waypoints, and replace the static geometric attention bias with a dynamic edge matrix fusing geometry, visual similarity and instruction relevance.
insight: Dense graphs are not automatically better: lowering the threshold statically to 0.25 increases nodes from 23.14 to 31.61 and slightly hurts R2R-CE performance, and a random threshold also fails. Gains come from the dispersion signal and from intervening only in complex scenes; conditional mapping beats global mapping (SR 58.56 vs 57.10). In the edge ablation, E_sem alone makes the agent efficient but less accurate (SR 55.85, SPL 49.52), and E_inst alone does not help (SR 56.01); combining them gives SR 58.56, so instruction relevance acts as a filter on visual shortcuts.
method: Waypoint dispersion metric: the standard deviation σ_t of the relative angles of candidate ghost nodes measures local scene complexity (high at intersections, low in corridors).

Adaptive threshold γ_t: a conditional linear inverse map keeps γ=0.5 m when σ_t ≤ σ_med and decreases linearly toward 0.25 m as σ_t rises to σ_max. Parameters are calibrated on the σ distribution from ETPNav on Val-Seen. It is used only at inference; training keeps γ fixed at 0.5 m.
Dynamic Edge Fusion: E_dynamic = E_geo + ω1·E_sem + ω2·E_inst. E_geo is normalized Euclidean distance; E_sem = MLP([v_i;v_j]); E_inst = w_i·w_j with w_i = MLP([v_i;W_L]).
Graph Transformer with dynamic bias: GASA layers add E_dynamic to the attention logits in place of the static geometric bias, giving soft semantic edges.
Feature encoders: BERT (R2R-CE) or RoBERTa (RxR-CE) for instructions, CLIP-ViT panoramic node features with orientation embeddings, and the ETPNav waypoint predictor and controller.
Training-variant exploration: node gating, geometric dropout and geometric annealing are tested as optional strategies, not used in the main model.

setting.backbone: ETPNav-style modular pipeline: CLIP-ViT + BERT/RoBERTa + Dynamic Graph Transformer (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE training sets, following the ETPNav two-stage protocol with pretrained ViT/BERT; no extra data reported
setting.action_space: Predicted waypoints on an online topological graph, executed by a low-level controller (turn 15°, forward 0.25 m)

numbers.extra: adaptive γ (0.25-0.5 m) at inference only
numbers.evidence: Table I, Ours (DGNav) Val-Unseen: 11.64 4.66 65 59 50 (Table III/IV give SR 58.56, SPL 50.08, OSR 64.82)

numbers_note: Table I prints R2R-CE SR/SPL/OSR as integers; the ablation tables give two-decimal values for val-unseen. In the Table VI training-variant ablation, the annealing variant reaches SR 59.11, OSR 67.43 and SPL 48.16 (not the main model).
results: DGNav improves on its direct baseline ETPNav on R2R-CE val-unseen (SR 57→59, SPL 49→50, NE 4.71→4.66) with about 0.4 more nodes on average. On RxR-CE val-unseen it improves nDTW (61.49→62.04) and SDTW (43.92→44.49). It trails Safe-VLN in SR on R2R-CE val-unseen (60 vs 59) but has higher SPL, and on test-unseen SPL drops 1 point vs ETPNav.
limitations: Gains over ETPNav are small (about 1-2 points), and test-unseen SPL is lower than ETPNav; on RxR-CE val-unseen NE gets worse (5.80→6.00).

The adaptive threshold is applied only at inference and its parameters are calibrated on ETPNav statistics from Val-Seen. It relies on a simple angular-dispersion proxy, with no train-time integration.
Evaluated only in simulation on R2R-CE and RxR-CE; the edge-fusion ablation is done only on R2R-CE.
